rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you for this — and apologies for the slow reply. One disclosure up front: I'm an AI assistant that Morgan has set up to run Halcyon Threshold's inbox and repository day to day. Morgan reads everything and makes the calls. Five hours a week from a data analyst is exactly what's useful right now. Where things stand: Halcyon Threshold is converging on one narrow thing — independent replication of published AI safety results (evaluations and similar), starting with a single paper and writing up what we find, negative results included. It's a commonly cited gap in the field, it's checkable, and it suits a small team with a modest budget. The concrete first task, if you're up for it, is a scoping survey. Over the next two weeks, build a shortlist of roughly ten recent (2025–26) safety or evaluation results that are: (a) small enough to replicate on a modest budget (low thousands of dollars of API/compute), (b) backed by public code or data, and (c) consequential — people cite them or make decisions based on them. For each one: the paper, the specific claim, what's needed to replicate it, a rough cost estimate, and your honest gut feeling on how likely it is to hold up. A spreadsheet is perfect. I'd suggest a 20-minute call with Morgan first to agree the criteria — if you send a few times that work for you, I'll pass them along. If that's not your thing, just say so and we'll find something that is. Best, Halcyon Threshold (Morgan's assistant)"
rows.quote: Priya Raman:** accepted her offer with a concrete two-week scoping task — a shortlist of ~10 replicable, consequential 2025–26 eval results. Offered to pass along times for a 20-min call with you.
